newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: S.America vegetable oil sales near record - trade.
newsitem.headline: S.America vegetable oil sales near record - trade.

text.p: South American vegetable oil sales are proceding at near record levels, but traders foresee a tight market until the new northern hemisphere crop.

"In June, Argentina and Brazil between them shipped 551,000 tonnes of soybean and sunflower oil. If that's not a record it's almost a record," one trader said, "Now the lineups for July are huge, South America has 430,000-440,000 tonnes combined soy and sunflower oil already nominated, and it's just the second day of the month."

The trader said that, while there had been a lull in volume in recent days with the Hong Kong handover and big falls in Chicago prices, South America has been doing constant business to most destinations and that this looked like continuing. "The Far East, India, the Mediterrenean, Latin America, it's all moving," he said, "This is in spite of the fact that the U.S. is competitive and some vessels will obviously shift north and load in the Gulf. But the Gulf sold out for July."
He added, "Oil markets will be tight until the northern hemisphere new crop kicks in, that's the way it looks."
Russia has been in the market buying sunflower seed oil, the trader said, with three ships carrying about 50,000-60,000 tonnes of crude oil already nominated.

"They need oil. Their new crop comes in September and until then they need imports," he said, "They regularly import refined and bottled sunoil from Bunge, but now they are out for crude and so far as I know three vessels have been nominated and one of those has already sailed."
He said the Russians were probably looking for another 10,000-20,000 tonnes of Argentine sunflower oil.
Another trader said that the Chinese and Iranians had been buying soybean oil.
But Argentine sunflower seed and soybeans are not currently competitive on international markets, and exports are thin.
"There's only been 20,000 tonnes of sunflower seed placed so far this season, It's not competitive against Europe," a trader said. "The soybeans aren't competitive against Brazil."

Exporters had placed 15,000 tonnes of sunflower seed and 500,000 tonnes of soybeans with foreign buyers by June 25, according to the latest government figures. The government forecasts total season exports of just 50,000 tonnes of sunflower seed and 600,000 tonnes of soybeans.
Traders quoted soybean oil for July shipment offered at $519 and bid at $515 FOB. Sunflower seed oil was bid for Augsut at $510.
